aide.essaiTitre: How does the free trial work?
aide.essaiSuite: When the trial ends you can stay on the free version or move to Glamia Pro for unlimited clients and advanced stats. Nothing is charged until you choose a plan.
aide.payTitre: Glamia Pay: how do I get paid?
aide.payTexte: From the app you can take card payments without a terminal (the card taps on your iPhone), ask for a deposit or hold a card at booking, and send a payment link by text. Everything is tracked in your Glamia balance. If a payment or a refund puzzles you, write to us and we will look at it with you.
aide.bugTexte: Close the app completely and open it again; if the problem is still there, sign out and sign back in. If that is not enough, write to contact@glamia.pro describing what happens (a screenshot helps): we answer quickly.
aide.supprimerCompteTexte: You can ask us to delete your account and all your data for good at any time, by writing to contact@glamia.pro from your account address. Deletion is carried out within a few days, in line with data protection law.
aide.clienteTexte: To change or cancel an appointment, use the booking link your professional shared with you, or contact her directly. For a technical problem with the online booking, write to contact@glamia.pro.

sections.titre: 1. Who we are, and what these Terms cover
paragraphes: Glamia is an appointment, client-management and payment application for beauty professionals. These Terms form a binding agreement between you and Glamia, and apply every time you access or use the application, the booking pages it generates, or any related service (together, the “Service”).
If you do not agree to these Terms, do not use the Service.

The Service is for business use by beauty professionals. By registering you confirm that you are at least 18 years old, that you have the authority to enter into these Terms, and that you are using the Service in the course of a trade, business or profession.
The Service is not intended for consumers acting outside a business. Your clients do not hold an account: they only use the booking page you publish.
You are responsible for keeping your login details confidential and for everything done through your account. Tell us immediately if you believe your account has been used without your permission.
You must give accurate registration information and keep it up to date. We may suspend an account whose details are false or misleading.
You agree to use the Service for its intended purpose: managing appointments, following up with clients, and taking payment for services you actually provide.
You must not:
liste: use the Service unlawfully, or to arrange anything unlawful;
upload content that is unlawful, abusive, or infringes anyone’s rights;
attempt to access data belonging to other professionals or their clients;
copy, resell, reverse-engineer or attempt to extract the source of the Service;
use the Service to send unsolicited marketing in breach of applicable law.

sections.titre: 5. Your clients’ data — your role and ours
paragraphes: You decide which client information you record and why. In data protection terms, you are the controller of your clients’ personal data, and Glamia acts as your processor: we handle that data on your instructions, to provide the Service.

You are responsible for having a lawful basis to record and use your clients’ data, and for telling them how it is used. We are responsible for keeping it secure and for only using it to run the Service.
Glamia is the controller of your own account data (your registration details, your subscription, your use of the app).
How all of this works in practice is set out in our {confidentialite}.

Glamia Pay lets you ask for a deposit, hold a card on file, take card payments and send payment links. Payments are processed by Stripe. Glamia is not a bank and never holds your money: funds move from your client to your own connected account.
You are responsible for the prices you set, for the cancellation and no-show terms you display to your clients, for issuing any refund you owe, and for your own tax and accounting obligations.

Where you charge a card on file for a no-show, you must have shown your client the conditions before she paid or authorised the card. Chargebacks and disputes raised by your clients are between you and your client; we will give you the records we hold to help you respond.
Paid plans are sold through the Apple App Store and billed by Apple. Renewals, cancellations and refunds follow Apple’s rules and your App Store account settings, not ours.
If your subscription lapses, your account moves to a limited state: your data is kept, but some features stop. We will tell you before that happens.

We work hard to keep the Service available and accurate, but we do not promise that it will be uninterrupted, error-free, or fit for any particular purpose beyond what these Terms describe. To the fullest extent permitted by law, we exclude all implied warranties.

The Service depends on third parties — Apple, Stripe, hosting and email providers, mobile networks. We are not responsible for their failures, though we will do what we reasonably can to limit the effect on you.

Nothing in these Terms limits or excludes our liability for death or personal injury caused by our negligence, for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or for anything else that cannot lawfully be limited or excluded.
Subject to that, and to the fullest extent permitted by law:
liste: we are not liable for loss of profit, loss of business, loss of goodwill, loss of anticipated savings, missed appointments, or any indirect or consequential loss;
we are not liable for loss or corruption of data beyond restoring the most recent backup we hold;

our total liability to you, for all claims arising in any twelve-month period, is limited to the greater of the amount you paid us for the Service in that period, or one hundred pounds sterling (or its equivalent in your currency).

paragraphes: You agree to cover us for any claim, loss, fine or reasonable cost we suffer because of the way you used the Service — in particular any claim from one of your clients, any breach of data protection law on your side, and any tax or consumer-law obligation of yours that you did not meet.
The Service — its design, code, brand and content — belongs to Glamia. These Terms give you permission to use it while your account is open; they do not transfer any ownership.

What you put into Glamia stays yours: your service names, your prices, your photos, your client records. You give us only the permission we need to display and process them in order to run the Service for you.
You may close your account at any time. You can export your client list before you go, including if your subscription has expired.

We may suspend or close an account that breaches these Terms, that puts other users or their clients at risk, or that we are required to act on by law. Where it is reasonable to do so, we will warn you first.

sections.titre: 1. Who is responsible for your data
paragraphes: Glamia is an appointment, client-management and payment application for beauty professionals.
There are two different situations, and they matter:

When you book an appointment with a professional, that professional decides what to record about you and why. She is the controller of your data. Glamia acts as her processor: we hold and handle it on her instructions, to run her booking page and her diary. Requests about your appointment record go to her first; we will help her answer.
When a professional creates a Glamia account, Glamia is the controller of her own account data.
When you book online, we collect:
liste: the services chosen, and the date and time of the appointment;
any optional comment or inspiration photo you send;
answers to any question your professional asks before booking.

paragraphes: If you pay online — a deposit, a card held on file, or a payment through Glamia Pay — we record the amount, the type and the date of the transaction, and technical payment references.
Your card details are entered and processed directly by Stripe, a payment provider certified to the PCI-DSS standard. They never pass through Glamia and are never stored on our servers.

When you leave a card on file, no money is taken at booking. It is an authorisation allowing your professional to charge the agreed amount if you do not turn up without cancelling, under the conditions shown to you before you authorised it.

sections.titre: 4. Why we use it, and on what basis
paragraphes: We use your data only to run the booking service: managing your appointment, sending confirmations and reminders, processing payments and refunds, and letting you and your professional communicate about the appointment.

If you are in the United Kingdom or the European Economic Area, our lawful bases are the performance of the service you asked for (Article 6(1)(b) UK GDPR / GDPR), our legal and accounting obligations for payment records (Article 6(1)(c)), and our legitimate interest in keeping the service secure and working (Article 6(1)(f)).
If you are in Canada, we collect and use your information with your knowledge and consent, for the purposes described here, as required by PIPEDA.
If you are in the United States, we process your information for the business purposes described here.

sections.titre: 5. We do not sell your data
paragraphes: We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising. We have not done so in the past twelve months. This statement is made for the purposes of the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended (CCPA/CPRA), and applies equally everywhere else.
Your data is accessible only to the professional you book with, and to the technical providers listed below.
We use technical providers strictly necessary to run the service:
liste: Hosting: Supabase, on servers located in the European Union.
Payments: Stripe, for secure processing of Glamia Pay transactions.
Email delivery: our emailing provider, for confirmations and reminders.
Push notifications: Expo, to alert your professional on her phone.

sections.titre: 7. Where your data is held, and transfers
paragraphes: Your data is hosted in the European Union.

For users in the United Kingdom, transfers rely on the UK’s adequacy regulations for the EEA. For users elsewhere, where a transfer is needed we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses or another lawful transfer mechanism, and we require our providers to protect your data to the same standard.
Your appointment data is kept for as long as you have a commercial relationship with your professional, then deleted within 12 months of your last appointment.
Payment and invoicing records are kept for as long as our legal and accounting obligations require, which may be longer.
Wherever you are, you can ask us to give you a copy of your data, correct it, or delete it. Depending on where you live you may also have the rights below.
United Kingdom and EEA: access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, and the right to object to processing based on legitimate interests.
Canada: access to your personal information, correction of inaccuracies, and withdrawal of consent, subject to legal and contractual limits.

California: the right to know what we collect and why, to delete it, to correct it, to opt out of sale or sharing (we do neither), and not to be treated differently for exercising any of these rights.
{contact}
The booking service is not intended for children under 16. We do not knowingly collect data from them. If you believe a child’s data has been recorded, write to us and we will remove it.
The Glamia booking site does not use advertising cookies. Only technical cookies necessary for the service to work are used.

Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Access is limited to what each part of the service needs. Card details are never held by us. No system is perfectly secure, but we will tell you and the relevant authority without undue delay if a breach affects your rights.

If you are not satisfied with how we handled your data, you can complain to your supervisory authority: the Information Commissioner’s Office in the United Kingdom, the Office of the Privacy Commissioner in Canada, your State Attorney General in the United States, or the CNIL in France.
